issue.entity: Shenzhen Hua Advanced Energy Manufacturing Co.
issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (East Asia)

plan.diagnosis: Shenzhen Hua Advanced Energy Manufacturing Co. presents a single-source sub-tier dependency risk with USD 4,789,423 annual spend concentrated in East Asia (CN). The supplier experienced 2 disruption events in the past 12 months and maintains a moderate resiliency score of 63 across 23 sub-tier suppliers, creating exposure to supply chain interruptions.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping audit with Shenzhen Hua to identify the critical single-source sub-tier supplier(s) among the 23 sub-tier vendors and document dependencies
Issue RFI to 3-5 alternative suppliers in alternate geographies (Southeast Asia, India, or Eastern Europe) capable of serving the identified sub-tier component need
Qualify and onboard at least one backup sub-tier supplier; negotiate contractual commitment from Shenzhen Hua to dual-source the critical sub-tier component
Implement 60-day safety stock buffer for critical components sourced through Shenzhen Hua until dual sub-tier sourcing is operational
Establish quarterly business continuity reviews with Shenzhen Hua including sub-tier risk monitoring and disruption mitigation protocols

plan.expected_impact: Mitigating single-source sub-tier risk will reduce potential disruption exposure of USD 4,789,423 annual spend and improve supply continuity for energy manufacturing components
kpis: Number of qualified alternate sub-tier suppliers (target: ≥1 within 90 days)
Sub-tier supplier geographic diversification index (target: <70% concentration in single region)
Resiliency score improvement (target: 63 to ≥75 within 6 months)
Disruption event frequency (target: reduce from 2 to 0 events per 12 months)
Safety stock days on hand for critical components (target: 60 days)
risks: Shenzhen Hua may resist sub-tier transparency or refuse to dual-source due to existing supplier relationships or cost impact
Qualifying alternate sub-tier suppliers may require 90-120 days, extending exposure window during 2 ongoing disruption event pattern
Safety stock investment will increase working capital by approximately 16% of USD 4,789,423 spend (USD 766,307) until dual-sourcing achieved
Geographic diversification may increase sub-tier component costs by 8-15%, requiring negotiation to share cost with Shenzhen Hua
erp_actions: SAP: Add source list entry (ME01) flagging Shenzhen Hua (vendor master) with sub-tier risk indicator and mandatory approval workflow for POs >USD 100K
Oracle EBS: Update supplier attribute in PO module to 'Medium Risk - Sub-tier Dependency' and require Procurement Manager approval for requisitions
Coupa: Create supplier risk flag in supplier record and configure automated notifications when PR/PO is created against this supplier
SAP: Extend payment terms from Net-30 to Net-45 (XK02 vendor master update) contingent on sub-tier transparency and dual-sourcing commitment
NetSuite/Dynamics 365: Add custom field 'Sub-tier Mapping Status' to vendor record and set required validation before PO approval until mapping complete
All ERPs: Establish spend alerts at 25% quarterly threshold (USD 1,197,356) to monitor concentration and trigger sourcing review
